Song — Playlist

MPC2000XL style: each Sequence (above) is one bar of steps + notes. A Song strings sequences together — add them in order, set how many bars each one plays, and the transport runs the chain instead of looping a single sequence. Edit a sequence any time; the playlist just points at it. Using the same SEQ in several steps reuses that one sequence — an edit shows in every step that uses it. For a variation, use ⧉ Duplicate in the rack instead: the copy is fully independent, so changing it never touches the original.
Pattern mode — SEQ 1 loops on its own.
While the song plays, Follow jumps the rack view to each sequence as it’s reached — turn it off to edit a different sequence without the view moving. In Song mode, Export renders the whole playlist chain.

    Piano Roll — 808

    No note selected — click a note block to select it.
    FL-style editing: click an empty cell to add a note · drag a note to move it (up/down = pitch, auditioned as you drag on pitched channels) · drag its right edge to change its length · right-click or long-press a note to delete it. Drum channels get the same treatment — their step-grid hits show as dashed blocks and become full notes the moment you drag, resize or set their velocity. In-key rows are tinted, roots are gold, out-of-key notes flag red on the 808. Tools (top right of the Piano Roll): Draw is the editing above. Eraser — tap a note to delete it, or drag across a run of notes to clear them all; no long-press needed, which is the reliable way to delete on a phone browser. Splitter — tap a note to cut it in two at the tapped spot, or drag a vertical line across stacked notes to cut every note it crosses at that same column; the cut follows the Snap setting (Snap on = nearest grid line, Snap off = the exact sub-step position tapped), both halves keep the original pitch and velocity, notes too short to split are left alone, and each tap or drag is a single undo step. Select — drag across the grid to marquee-select some or all notes, click a note to select just it, drag any selected note to move the whole selection together (relative positions kept), Delete removes the selection; a group move or delete is one undo step. The grid's lines are the Snap setting — change Snap and the divisions redraw to match. The teal line sweeping the grid in playback is the playhead, and the keyboard under the roll lights each note as it sounds. Voices (top right, beside Root note) is the channel's polyphony: Poly lets notes ring over each other; Mono (the MPC 2000's word) cuts the ringing voice the moment a new note lands — the setting for 808s and sounds that must never overlap. Pitch detection: every sample you assign is analysed and its pitch is reported in the header (⟳ Re-detect re-runs it) — for tuning and the key guide only. Like FL Studio, detection never moves a root: every channel's root is C5 unless you move it with the Root Note control, so the same key plays the same pitch in both apps. A chop/loop's detected key sets the project key, and a sound with no clear pitch says so instead of guessing. Key guide (top right) is off unless you call it: on, the project key's scale rows light with the root strongest, out-of-key rows dim, and the keyboard marks its in-key keys — guidance only, nothing is ever blocked.

    Sampler — MPC Loops

    Feed it any audio — a stem, a song, a one-shot. It finds the tempo and the 1, locks a loop of any bar count that starts and stops exactly, and plays it back with no pops. Exports start exactly on the 1 and end exactly at the loop end — ready to zone on the MPC.

    Lock a loop to see its exact length.

    Send it into the beat

    A send renders the loop exactly like an export — exactly N bars starting exactly on the 1, no silent head, at the sample rate picked above — and builds the channel in Beat Lab with the audio loaded: a wave channel gets it as a clip at the top of its lane; a sequencer channel gets it as its one-shot sample. Undo removes a sent channel like any other.
    How the 1 is found: leading silence is trimmed by the gate, the beat grid is phase-aligned to the strongest hits, and the first full bar from there is bar 1. Sparse material — a lone bassline, horns with no drums — can fool any detector: the BPM box, ÷2/×2, and the nudge buttons are there so your ear stays the final judge. Use the ruler-drag to slide the start close, then drag the gold In/Out bars on the wave — snapped to the grid, or free with snap off — to place it exactly.
